message.content: Should auto-add survive v2? Read the PRD and Ravi's eval notes and tell me where we stand.

content.text:
Short version: on the numbers, auto-add can't survive v2 as it is.

- **The model**: 81.0% of spines read correctly (1,004 of 1,240 photos, 96 shelves). Ravi's own threshold for auto-add is 95%.
- **Where it misses**: tilted spines 34%, glare 27%, thin spines 21%, stacked or sideways books 12%, other 6% of the 236 wrong reads. Confidence doesn't separate right from wrong well, so a threshold on it won't fix this.
- **The PRD today**: Requirements say nothing is added until the steward taps "Add", but Open question Q1 still asks whether to keep auto-add for stewards whose scans are 95%+ accurate.
- **Caveat**: the glare set is only 140 photos from 9 shelves, so treat the glare share as soft.

I'd leave Q1 open until we have the beta evidence next to the eval. Want me to check the two against each other?

message.content: Check the eval numbers against the beta feedback, then add a What we heard section to the PRD.

- 81.0% of spines read correctly, and glare alone causes 27% of the wrong reads.
- Three of eight testers (P3, P6, P8) stopped scanning after a wrong book was added for them.

One thing needs your call before I touch the goals or Open questions.

questions.question: Three testers (P3, P6, P8) say a wrong auto-added book is why they stopped scanning. That conflicts with v1 goal 2, "every scanned spine lands in the catalog with no extra taps". Put auto-add behind the review step, or keep it and log an open question?
